name: 灰喉針尾雨燕

similarSpecies.distinction: Sexes similar. Dark blue-gloss brown, PALE SILVERY GREY SADDLE on back, broad sharply contrasting WHITE THROAT plus WHITE LORES/FOREHEAD BAND. White horseshoe rear flanks/undertail around dark belly, short square tail tiny needle spines only close views. caudacutus central Siberia to Sakhalin/Kurils/Mongolia/NE China/Korea/Japan breeding, winters S New Guinea/E Australia; nudipes N Pakistan/Himalaya/N Myanmar/SW China, winter poorly known possibly Malaya/Java. LC stable globally; scarce HK spring migrant declined locally since1990s, not a global IUCN trend.

Brown-backed Needletail indicus representation, pale BROWN rather than silvery grey saddle, dark brown throat paler chin, small white loral spot, long full body broad wings short square needle-spined tail and white horseshoe. LC decreasing; not to scale.

rangeMap.note: Sexes similar. Dark blue-gloss brown with pale SILVERY GREY SADDLE. ILL-DEFINED DUSKY GREY BROWN THROAT and DARK FOREHEAD unlike white-throated. White horseshoe rear flank/undertail and short square needle-spined tail. Distant birds very hard to separate; close head/throat views important. Monotypic breeds central Nepal/NE India/N Myanmar/S China to E Guangxi/Hainan/Taiwan, winters Thailand/Malay peninsula/Sumatra/W Java. LC stable globally; scarce HK spring passage declined locally since1990s. World partial native-country overview only; green does not mean entire country occupancy, precise occurrence or complete range.
